subject: How to procrustes align data assuming object symetry

messages.author: b35f414539b34a6c
messages.subject: How to procrustes align data assuming object symetry
parts:
Hey all,

So in Chris Kilingenberg's Morphoj when you import a dataset there's an option of specifying that your observations are symmetrical (i think it specifically means object symmetry). It then asks you to pair a few landmarks and infers the rest. Then when you Procrustes align the data it takes that into account. 

How do i get that in geomorph? 

When i align the data in both programs (in geomorph i use gpagen), the mean Procrustes coordinates are different. I also tried the bilat.symmetry function but the numbers given by Morphoj do not match either the symmetrical or asymmetrical components produced by this function.

The fact that they don't match makes me think i'm missing something when aligning my data in geomorph. For context: I'm studying facial photos so there is object symmetry.

Thanks for any help,

Richie

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] How to procrustes align data assuming object symetry
parts:
Richie,

 

See the help page for bilat.symmetry. It provides instructions on what is required. Also, the geomorph manual found on Github provides additional guidance.


Regarding MorphoJ: Yes, things will be slightly different, due to some computational decisions made in MorphoJ. For instance, MorphoJ uses Full Procrustes fitting whereas virtually all other morphometyric software for which I am aware (including geomorph) use the standard Partial Procrustes fitting.  Thus, values will not be numerically identical in MorphoJ following alignment. However, there will be a perfect 1.0 correlation between geomorph and TPSRelw for example, in terms of estimated shape differences found from GPA-aligned shapes. Other procedural choices in MorphoJ can also cause some slight differences for particular analyses.

 

Dean
